Turkish Airlines Baggage Allowance 2026: Weight, Pieces & Fees

Turkish Airlines splits its checked baggage rules into two separate systems depending on where you're flying. On routes to the Americas, you get a  piece allowance  (2 bags up to 23 kg each in Economy). On routes within Europe, Asia and the Middle East, you get a  weight allowance  that can total 15-30 kg depending on your fare. Carry-on is one cabin bag (55 × 40 × 23 cm, 8 kg) plus a personal item, regardless of route. Mixing up the two systems is a common source of unexpected excess baggage fees on this airline.

TL;DR — Turkish Airlines Baggage at a Glance

Americas routes (piece concept):  Economy 2 × 23 kg, Business 2 × 32 kg

Europe/Asia/Middle East (weight concept):  Economy 15-30 kg total depending on fare, Business 30-40 kg

Carry-on:  1 bag, 55 × 40 × 23 cm, max 8 kg + 1 personal item, 40 × 30 × 15 cm, max 4 kg

Students (12-34, international):  up to 40 kg or 2 × 23 kg with valid Miles&Smiles + annual proof of enrollment

Price reference:  JFK– Istanbul  round-trip Economy on Turkish Airlines showed around $2,378 for December 2026 departures in SkySonar's live price tracker as of October 2026 — fares change daily, so check current prices before booking

Which baggage system applies to my route?

Turkish Airlines uses the  piece concept  on flights to and from the Americas (US, Canada, Latin America) — you're allowed a set number of bags regardless of total weight, up to 23 kg per bag in Economy. Everywhere else — Europe, Asia, Middle East, Africa, Turkey domestic — it uses the  weight concept , where your ticket comes with a total kg budget you can split across any number of bags. Check your e-ticket or booking confirmation; the allowance is listed next to each flight segment, and it can change mid-itinerary on connecting flights.

How much can I check in Economy class?

On piece-concept routes, Economy includes  2 checked bags, 23 kg each  (46 kg total, but never combine the two into one bag over 23 kg). On weight-concept routes, Economy allowance depends on fare: EcoFly gives 15-20 kg, ExtraFly 20-30 kg, FlexiFly up to 30 kg. Domestic Turkey flights follow the same fare-tier logic, starting at 15 kg on EcoFly.

Fly to Istanbul and onward to Asia and you’re on “weight concept”: one total number of kilos you can split across any number of bags. Fly through Istanbul to New York and you’re on “piece concept”: a fixed number of bags, each capped separately. Book the wrong fare for the wrong system and you either overpack a bag you’re allowed or get stung for a second one you assumed was included.

The cabin side, at least, is refreshingly generous. This guide covers the carry-on rules, the personal item allowance, how each fare and route concept changes your checked allowance, Miles&Smiles bonuses, infant rules, and what to do when a bag doesn’t turn up in Istanbul.

Economy checked (weight concept routes): typically 30 kg, split across any number of bags

Economy checked (piece concept routes — Americas, parts of Africa): 2 x 23 kg

TRAVEL INTEL

Istanbul Airport minimum connection time: 2.5 hours, not 90 minutes

By ATC Intelligence ,  Published July 25, 2026

Quick summary

Istanbul Airport’s published minimum connection time is 45 minutes for domestic-to-domestic flights and 75 to 90 minutes for international-to-international transfers, but those are airline scheduling figures. The buffer that holds in practice is 2.5 hours between opposite international piers, 2.5 to 3 hours when passport control is involved, and 3 hours for a two-airline interline ticket.

🏢 Terminal Guide & Navigation

Istanbul Airport operates from one massive terminal building with 1,440,000 m² floor space, making it the world's third-largest airport terminal. The terminal is divided into five concourses: A, B, D, and F handle international flights, while pier G and three areas of pier F serve domestic flights. Each concourse has 8-17 gates, with walking times from central terminal to the furthest gates (A11, B15, D17, F16, G11) requiring 15-20 minutes due to the terminal's enormous scale. Moving walkways are available but insufficient for the distances involved, requiring passengers to arrive 2.5-3 hours before flights.  Security processing features separate checkpoints for domestic and international flights, staffed by 3,500 security personnel and 750 immigration officers providing comprehensive processing capabilities. Immigration and passport controls are located in both arrivals and departures areas with clear directional signage. Turkish Airlines operates this as their primary hub with over 50 airlines serving 122 countries, making it a major transcontinental connection point between Europe, Asia, and beyond.  The terminal houses five 24-hour lounges including three Turkish Airlines lounges (Domestic, International, and Business), plus IGA Lounge and SkyTeam Lounge. Dining and shopping options include over 100 establishments ranging from local Turkish cuisine at Simit Sarayi to international brands like Burger King and Starbucks, plus extensive duty-free shopping featuring clothing, electronics, and Turkish specialties. Family facilities include dedicated check-in areas in aisle K, children's play areas in the CIP Lounge, nursing rooms, and complimentary buggy services for families with children 0-2, expectant mothers, and passengers over 65. The airport opened in 2019 as Turkey's new aviation flagship, replacing the older Atatürk Airport as Istanbul's primary international gateway.

When you're connecting through Istanbul's Sabiha Gokcen or Istanbul Airport, understanding the minimum connection time and how to arrange a transfer is crucial to avoid missing your next flight. The istanbul airport minimum connection time transfer depends on whether you're connecting domestically or internationally, and getting the right ground transportation can make the difference between a smooth journey and a stressful rush.

Understanding Minimum Connection Time at Istanbul Airports

Istanbul has two major airports: Istanbul Airport (IST), located on the European side about 25 kilometers from the city center, and Sabiha Gokcen International Airport (SAW), situated on the Asian side roughly 50 kilometers away. Each airport has different minimum connection time (MCT) requirements based on your itinerary.

At Istanbul Airport (IST), the minimum connection time is typically 90 minutes for domestic to domestic connections, and 120 minutes for international to international or mixed connections. At Sabiha Gokcen, these times are similar, though some airlines may require slightly longer windows depending on their terminal and baggage handling procedures.

These official times assume you're working with direct baggage handling and normal circumstances. However, if you're arranging your own transfer between flights, you'll need to add significant buffer time to account for ground transportation, immigration, customs, and the unpredictability of traffic in Istanbul.

Why Transfer Time Matters for Connecting Passengers

A minimum connection time is the shortest period airlines calculate between your arrival and departure, assuming your inbound flight is on time and your luggage is checked through to your final destination. If you're arriving with checked baggage that needs to be collected and re-checked, or if you're connecting between different airlines, you'll need longer than the MCT.

When you book a transfer as a connecting passenger, you're adding an extra variable to your journey. Unlike a direct baggage handoff, you must physically exit the terminal, clear immigration (if required), and arrange ground transportation to either leave the airport area or move between terminals. This is why many travel experts recommend at least 180 to 240 minutes (3 to 4 hours) for international to international connections with a separate transfer booking.

Transfer Options for Connecting Passengers

If you have a long layover, you might consider leaving the airport entirely. An  istanbul airport transfer  can take you to Istanbul's city center in 30 to 45 minutes under normal traffic conditions. The minimum connection time commonly published for Istanbul Airport is 90 minutes for an international-to-international connection, 45 minutes for domestic-to-domestic, and around 120 minutes when your two flights are on different airlines on the same ticket. Individual carriers file their own figures and Turkish Airlines is frequently quoted between 60 and 75 minutes, so check the number that applies to your booking.

That figure is the shortest layover an airline will sell you at Istanbul on a single ticket. It is a scheduling rule, not a prediction. What makes Istanbul different from most hubs is not a terminal change or a border crossing. It is sheer scale. The terminal is a single building roughly 1.4 kilometres (0.9 miles) end to end, and the fixed costs of arriving there, taxiing, deplaning and walking to the central hub, can consume 40 minutes before your connection has meaningfully begun.

Cappadocia in Winter — December, January & February Travel Guide

Skip to content

Table of Contents

Overview

Winter in Cappadocia is a well-kept secret among seasoned travelers. From December through February, the surreal rock formations and fairy chimneys are blanketed in snow, creating a landscape that feels lifted from a storybook. The crowds that pack Goreme in summer are almost entirely absent, and the silence across the valleys is striking.  This is the most affordable time to visit. Hotel rates drop 30-50% compared to peak season, tour operators offer winter specials, and balloon flight prices sit at their annual low. Cave hotels — already atmospheric year-round — become genuinely magical, with stone fireplaces crackling, heated floors warming your feet, and panoramic terraces framing snow-covered vistas.  The trade-off is weather-related uncertainty. Balloon flights have a higher cancellation rate in winter, roads can be icy after snowfall, and daylight hours are shorter. But for travelers willing to embrace the cold, winter Cappadocia delivers some of the most dramatic and intimate experiences the region has to offer. When a balloon does launch over a snow-white landscape at sunrise, it is, without exaggeration, one of the most spectacular sights in Turkey.

Pro Tip  The New Year period (December 25 - January 2) is the one winter window when prices spike and availability tightens. If you can travel in mid-January or February instead, you will get even lower rates and a quieter experience.

Weather by Month

Month  Avg High  Avg Low  Snowfall  Wind  Daylight Hours

December  4°C - 6°C  -3°C - -1°C  5-8 days  Moderate to strong  ~9.5 hours

January  2°C - 4°C  -5°C - -3°C  6-10 days  Strong  ~9.5 hours

February  3°C - 6°C  -4°C - -2°C  5-8 days  Moderate  ~10.5 hours

Understanding Winter Weather

Cappadocia sits at roughly 1,000 meters above sea level on the Anatolian plateau, giving it a continental climate with genuinely cold winters. Overnight temperatures regularly dip below -5°C in January, and daytime highs rarely climb above 6°C from December through February. Wind chill can make it feel significantly colder, especially on exposed ridges and valleys.  Snowfall is common but not constant. Cappadocia typically sees snow on 15 to 25 days across the winter season, though heavy accumulation is intermittent. A fresh snowfall can transform the landscape overnight, coating the fairy chimneys and valleys in white — these mornings are the most prized by photographers and balloon passengers alike.  Cloud cover is frequent, particularly in December and January. February tends to bring slightly more sunshine and the first hints that spring is approaching, with daylight stretching past 10.5 hours by the end of the month.

Two Airports, One Decision

If you're planning a trip to Cappadocia, one of the first practical questions you'll face is:  should I fly into Kayseri or Nevşehir?  It's a fair question -- Cappadocia is served by two airports, and choosing the right one can affect your schedule, budget, and overall travel experience.

Kayseri Erkilet Airport (IATA: ASR) is the larger, busier airport located about 75 km west of Göreme. Nevşehir Kapadokya Airport (IATA: NAV) is smaller and closer to the Cappadocia tourist zone at roughly 40 km from Göreme. On paper, Nevşehir sounds like the obvious winner -- but the reality is more nuanced.

In this guide, we'll break down everything you need to know about both airports with real, up-to-date information so you can make the right call for your trip.

Kayseri is well-served by multiple Turkish carriers. You'll find  8 to 12 daily flights from Istanbul , departing from both Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökcen Airport (SAW). The airlines operating regular routes include:

Turkish Airlines  -- Multiple daily flights from IST, full-service carrier with included baggage

Pegasus Airlines  -- Budget-friendly flights from SAW, often the cheapest option

AnadoluJet  -- Turkish Airlines' subsidiary with competitive fares from both IST and SAW

SunExpress  -- Seasonal and regular flights, sometimes from European cities

Beyond Istanbul, Kayseri also receives flights from  Ankara, Izmir, and Antalya , giving travelers connecting from other Turkish cities plenty of options. Some seasonal international charter flights also land here during peak tourist months.

Terminal Facilities

Kayseri's terminal is modern and well-equipped for a regional airport. You'll find ATMs and currency exchange offices in the arrivals hall, car rental desks from major agencies, a few cafes and shops, and free Wi-Fi.

Turkish Airlines Baggage Allowance 2026: Weight, Pieces & Fees

Turkish Airlines splits its checked baggage rules into two separate systems depending on where you're flying. On routes to the Americas, you get a  piece allowance  (2 bags up to 23 kg each in Economy). On routes within Europe, Asia and the Middle East, you get a  weight allowance  that can total 15-30 kg depending on your fare. Carry-on is one cabin bag (55 × 40 × 23 cm, 8 kg) plus a personal item, regardless of route. Mixing up the two systems is a common source of unexpected excess baggage fees on this airline.

TL;DR — Turkish Airlines Baggage at a Glance

Americas routes (piece concept):  Economy 2 × 23 kg, Business 2 × 32 kg

Europe/Asia/Middle East (weight concept):  Economy 15-30 kg total depending on fare, Business 30-40 kg

Carry-on:  1 bag, 55 × 40 × 23 cm, max 8 kg + 1 personal item, 40 × 30 × 15 cm, max 4 kg

Max weight per checked piece:  32 kg (heavier bags must be split into two)

Students (12-34, international):  up to 40 kg or 2 × 23 kg with valid Miles&Smiles + annual proof of enrollment

Price reference:  JFK– Istanbul  round-trip Economy on Turkish Airlines showed around $2,378 for December 2026 departures in SkySonar's live price tracker as of October 2026 — fares change daily, so check current prices before booking

Which baggage system applies to my route?

Turkish Airlines uses the  piece concept  on flights to and from the Americas (US, Canada, Latin America) — you're allowed a set number of bags regardless of total weight, up to 23 kg per bag in Economy. Everywhere else — Europe, Asia, Middle East, Africa, Turkey domestic — it uses the  weight concept , where your ticket comes with a total kg budget you can split across any number of bags. Check your e-ticket or booking confirmation; the allowance is listed next to each flight segment, and it can change mid-itinerary on connecting flights.

How much can I check in Economy class?

On piece-concept routes, Economy includes  2 checked bags, 23 kg each  (46 kg total, but never combine the two into one bag over 23 kg). On weight-concept routes, Economy allowance depends on fare: EcoFly gives 15-20 kg, ExtraFly 20-30 kg, FlexiFly up to 30 kg. Domestic Turkey flights follow the same fare-tier logic, starting at 15 kg on EcoFly.

Economy carry-on is 8 kg (55×40×23 cm); checked allowance ranges from 15 kg (EcoFly domestic) to 2×32 kg (Business Class international). The airline uses both weight-based and piece-based systems depending on the destination.

Flying through Istanbul Airport which handled a record-breaking 289,260 passengers on August 1, 2026 means Turkish Airlines is more popular than ever. With 358 destinations across 133 countries and a fleet of 563 aircraft, the carrier serves an enormous range of travelers. That scale also means its baggage rules aren’t one-size-fits-all.

Domestic flights follow different rules than international ones. Economy fares are split into four sub-types, each with its own baggage allowance. Piece-based routes to North America play by different rules than weight-based routes to Europe. Getting any of these wrong at the airport can cost you significantly.

What Is Turkish Airlines’ Carry-On Baggage Allowance in 2026?

Turkish Airlines allows Economy passengers one cabin bag (max 55×40×23 cm, 8 kg) plus one personal item (max 40×30×15 cm, 4 kg). Business Class passengers may bring two cabin bags, each 8 kg, totaling no more than 16 kg, plus one personal item of the same dimensions.

Turkish Airlines runs one of the more confusing baggage systems of any airline UK travellers use regularly. The rules themselves aren’t harsh; there are just two separate sets of them. Fly to Istanbul and onward to Asia and you’re on “weight concept”: one total number of kilos you can split across any number of bags. Fly through Istanbul to New York and you’re on “piece concept”: a fixed number of bags, each capped separately. Book the wrong fare for the wrong system and you either overpack a bag you’re allowed or get stung for a second one you assumed was included.

The cabin side, at least, is refreshingly generous. This guide covers the carry-on rules, the personal item allowance, how each fare and route concept changes your checked allowance, Miles&Smiles bonuses, infant rules, and what to do when a bag doesn’t turn up in Istanbul.

Quick answer:

Economy cabin bag: 55 x 40 x 23 cm, 8 kg — one of the larger free carry-ons in the sky

Economy personal item: 40 x 30 x 15 cm, up to 4 kg — under the seat in front

Business cabin: 2 bags, each 55 x 40 x 23 cm and 8 kg, plus a personal item

Economy checked (weight concept routes): typically 30 kg, split across any number of bags

Economy checked (piece concept routes — Americas, parts of Africa): 2 x 23 kg

Business checked: 40 kg (weight concept) / 2 x 32 kg (piece concept)

Piece concept applies to the Americas and several African routes; weight concept applies everywhere else, including UK–Istanbul

Carry-on bag : up to 55 x 40 x 23 cm including handles, wheels, and pockets, 8 kg maximum

Quick summary

Istanbul Airport’s published minimum connection time is 45 minutes for domestic-to-domestic flights and 75 to 90 minutes for international-to-international transfers, but those are airline scheduling figures. The buffer that holds in practice is 2.5 hours between opposite international piers, 2.5 to 3 hours when passport control is involved, and 3 hours for a two-airline interline ticket.

Queues peak between 05:00 and 08:00 and again from 21:00 to 01:00. On separate tickets no airline owes you a rebooking, so the buffer you buy is the only protection you have.

🏢 Terminal Guide & Navigation

Istanbul Airport operates from one massive terminal building with 1,440,000 m² floor space, making it the world's third-largest airport terminal. The terminal is divided into five concourses: A, B, D, and F handle international flights, while pier G and three areas of pier F serve domestic flights. Each concourse has 8-17 gates, with walking times from central terminal to the furthest gates (A11, B15, D17, F16, G11) requiring 15-20 minutes due to the terminal's enormous scale. Moving walkways are available but insufficient for the distances involved, requiring passengers to arrive 2.5-3 hours before flights.  Security processing features separate checkpoints for domestic and international flights, staffed by 3,500 security personnel and 750 immigration officers providing comprehensive processing capabilities. Immigration and passport controls are located in both arrivals and departures areas with clear directional signage. Turkish Airlines operates this as their primary hub with over 50 airlines serving 122 countries, making it a major transcontinental connection point between Europe, Asia, and beyond.  The terminal houses five 24-hour lounges including three Turkish Airlines lounges (Domestic, International, and Business), plus IGA Lounge and SkyTeam Lounge. Dining and shopping options include over 100 establishments ranging from local Turkish cuisine at Simit Sarayi to international brands like Burger King and Starbucks, plus extensive duty-free shopping featuring clothing, electronics, and Turkish specialties. Family facilities include dedicated check-in areas in aisle K, children's play areas in the CIP Lounge, nursing rooms, and complimentary buggy services for families with children 0-2, expectant mothers, and passengers over 65. The airport opened in 2019 as Turkey's new aviation flagship, replacing the older Atatürk Airport as Istanbul's primary international gateway.

When you're connecting through Istanbul's Sabiha Gokcen or Istanbul Airport, understanding the minimum connection time and how to arrange a transfer is crucial to avoid missing your next flight. The istanbul airport minimum connection time transfer depends on whether you're connecting domestically or internationally, and getting the right ground transportation can make the difference between a smooth journey and a stressful rush.

Understanding Minimum Connection Time at Istanbul Airports

Istanbul has two major airports: Istanbul Airport (IST), located on the European side about 25 kilometers from the city center, and Sabiha Gokcen International Airport (SAW), situated on the Asian side roughly 50 kilometers away. Each airport has different minimum connection time (MCT) requirements based on your itinerary.

At Istanbul Airport (IST), the minimum connection time is typically 90 minutes for domestic to domestic connections, and 120 minutes for international to international or mixed connections. At Sabiha Gokcen, these times are similar, though some airlines may require slightly longer windows depending on their terminal and baggage handling procedures.

These official times assume you're working with direct baggage handling and normal circumstances. However, if you're arranging your own transfer between flights, you'll need to add significant buffer time to account for ground transportation, immigration, customs, and the unpredictability of traffic in Istanbul.

Why Transfer Time Matters for Connecting Passengers

A minimum connection time is the shortest period airlines calculate between your arrival and departure, assuming your inbound flight is on time and your luggage is checked through to your final destination. If you're arriving with checked baggage that needs to be collected and re-checked, or if you're connecting between different airlines, you'll need longer than the MCT.

When you book a transfer as a connecting passenger, you're adding an extra variable to your journey. Unlike a direct baggage handoff, you must physically exit the terminal, clear immigration (if required), and arrange ground transportation to either leave the airport area or move between terminals. This is why many travel experts recommend at least 180 to 240 minutes (3 to 4 hours) for international to international connections with a separate transfer booking.

Transfer Options for Connecting Passengers

If you have a long layover, you might consider leaving the airport entirely. An  istanbul airport transfer  can take you to Istanbul's city center in 30 to 45 minutes under normal traffic conditions. Individual carriers file shorter figures, and Turkish Airlines is often quoted at 60 to 75 minutes. The minimum connection time commonly published for Istanbul Airport is 90 minutes for an international-to-international connection, 45 minutes for domestic-to-domestic, and around 120 minutes when your two flights are on different airlines on the same ticket. Individual carriers file their own figures and Turkish Airlines is frequently quoted between 60 and 75 minutes, so check the number that applies to your booking.

That figure is the shortest layover an airline will sell you at Istanbul on a single ticket. It is a scheduling rule, not a prediction. What makes Istanbul different from most hubs is not a terminal change or a border crossing. It is sheer scale. The terminal is a single building roughly 1.4 kilometres (0.9 miles) end to end, and the fixed costs of arriving there, taxiing, deplaning and walking to the central hub, can consume 40 minutes before your connection has meaningfully begun.

Cappadocia in Winter — December, January & February Travel Guide

Skip to content

Table of Contents

Overview

Winter in Cappadocia is a well-kept secret among seasoned travelers. From December through February, the surreal rock formations and fairy chimneys are blanketed in snow, creating a landscape that feels lifted from a storybook. The crowds that pack Goreme in summer are almost entirely absent, and the silence across the valleys is striking.  This is the most affordable time to visit. Hotel rates drop 30-50% compared to peak season, tour operators offer winter specials, and balloon flight prices sit at their annual low. Cave hotels — already atmospheric year-round — become genuinely magical, with stone fireplaces crackling, heated floors warming your feet, and panoramic terraces framing snow-covered vistas.  The trade-off is weather-related uncertainty. Balloon flights have a higher cancellation rate in winter, roads can be icy after snowfall, and daylight hours are shorter. But for travelers willing to embrace the cold, winter Cappadocia delivers some of the most dramatic and intimate experiences the region has to offer. When a balloon does launch over a snow-white landscape at sunrise, it is, without exaggeration, one of the most spectacular sights in Turkey.

Pro Tip  The New Year period (December 25 - January 2) is the one winter window when prices spike and availability tightens. If you can travel in mid-January or February instead, you will get even lower rates and a quieter experience.

Weather by Month

Month  Avg High  Avg Low  Snowfall  Wind  Daylight Hours

December  4°C - 6°C  -3°C - -1°C  5-8 days  Moderate to strong  ~9.5 hours

January  2°C - 4°C  -5°C - -3°C  6-10 days  Strong  ~9.5 hours

February  3°C - 6°C  -4°C - -2°C  5-8 days  Moderate  ~10.5 hours

Understanding Winter Weather

Cappadocia sits at roughly 1,000 meters above sea level on the Anatolian plateau, giving it a continental climate with genuinely cold winters. Overnight temperatures regularly dip below -5°C in January, and daytime highs rarely climb above 6°C from December through February. Wind chill can make it feel significantly colder, especially on exposed ridges and valleys.  Snowfall is common but not constant. Cappadocia typically sees snow on 15 to 25 days across the winter season, though heavy accumulation is intermittent.
